policy_title: Strengthen Parental Rights in School Curriculum
stated: The Conservative Party will deliver new legislation to make clear that parents have a right to see what their child is being taught in school and that schools must share all materials, especially on sensitive matters like relationships and sex education, and guarantee gender identity is not taught to children.

source.quote: We will work to strengthen the relationship between schools and parents, including by delivering new legislation which will make clear, beyond all doubt, that parents have a right to see what their child is being taught in school and schools must share all materials, especially on sensitive matters like relationships and sex education. ...and guarantee the contested concept of gender identity is not taught to children.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly shapes school curriculum content — restricting what is taught on gender identity and mandating parental access to teaching materials — producing a real verdict on school standards, curriculum scope, and potentially the attainment/inclusion gap for affected pupils.

Prohibiting gender identity from being taught raises genuine equal-treatment and anti-discrimination questions for LGBTQ+ children and families, and legislating parental override of curriculum content touches the civil-rights boundary between parental rights and pupils' own rights — both squarely within O9's strict scope.

Legislation banning specific curriculum content (gender identity) constitutes state coercion restricting educators' professional speech and curricular autonomy; the state mandating what schools are prohibited from teaching directly worsens freedom of expression in an institutional setting.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O7 for the direct curriculum and school-governance effect; O9 for differential treatment of a minority group in the educational setting; O10 for the state prohibition on specific speech/content in schools. O15 (belonging for LGBTQ+ students) is real but is already substantially captured by O9's minority-protections indicator, and the social-trust mechanism is too attenuated to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
